CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

Use when user says "diagnose this" / "debug this", reports a bug, says something is broken/throwing/failing, or describes a performance regression.

92				// browserAuthFlow interface (func types are invariant, so the
93				// method value alone won't do). On error the flow is a typed nil,
94				// which is fine — runLoginAuto checks err before touching it.
95				startBrowser := func(ctx context.Context) (browserAuthFlow, error) {

113	// parseLoginServer validates and canonicalises the --server value: an
114	// http(s) origin with nothing but scheme and host. Userinfo, path, query,
115	// and fragment are rejected rather than silently dropped — the value
116	// becomes the OAuth issuer, the token-exchange target, and the keyring
117	// key, so surprising rewrites would surface as confusing auth failures
118	// much later. A lone trailing slash is tolerated (normalised away).
119	func parseLoginServer(raw string) (string, error) {
120		raw = strings.TrimSpace(raw)
121		if raw == "" {
122			return "", errors.New("empty server URL")
123		}
124		u, err := url.Parse(raw)
125		if err != nil {
126			return "", fmt.Errorf("parse server URL: %w", err)
127		}
128		// Error messages echo u.Redacted(), not raw: the URL may carry
129		// userinfo (that's one of the rejection cases), and stderr often ends
130		// up in CI logs where a password must not appear.
131		switch {
132		case u.Scheme != schemeHTTPS && u.Scheme != schemeHTTP:
133			return "", fmt.Errorf("scheme must be http or https, got %q", u.Redacted())
134		case u.Host == "":
135			return "", fmt.Errorf("missing host in %q", u.Redacted())
136		case u.User != nil:
137			return "", fmt.Errorf("userinfo not allowed in %q", u.Redacted())
138		case u.Path != "" && u.Path != "/":
139			return "", fmt.Errorf("path not allowed in %q (use the bare origin)", u.Redacted())
140		case u.RawQuery != "" || u.Fragment != "":
141			return "", fmt.Errorf("query/fragment not allowed in %q", u.Redacted())
142		}
143		return api.NormalizeOriginURL(raw), nil
144	}

175			fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Login URL:   %s\n\n", approvalURL)
176			fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Press Enter to open in browser...")
177	
178			// Read from /dev/tty so we get a real keypress and don't consume piped stdin.
179			if err := waitForEnter(ctx); err != nil {
180				return fmt.Errorf("wait for input: %w", err)
181			}
182	
183			fmt.Fprintln(outW)
184			if err := openURL(ctx, approvalURL); err != nil {
185				fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Warning: failed to open browser: %v\n", err)
186				fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Open this URL in your browser to approve this login: %s\n", approvalURL)
187			}
188		} else {
189			fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Login URL:   %s\n\n", approvalURL)
190		}
191	
192		fmt.Fprint(outW, "Waiting for approval... ")
193	
194		token, refreshToken, err := waitForApproval(ctx, client, start.DeviceCode, start.ExpiresIn, time.Duration(start.Interval)*time.Second, defaultSlowDownBackoff)
195		if err != nil {
196			return fmt.Errorf("complete login: %w", err)
197		}
198	
199		return persistLogin(outW, client.BaseURL(), token, refreshToken)
200	}
201	
202	// loginFlowFacts carries the environment facts that pick between the
203	// browser and device-code flows. Detection happens once at the command
204	// entry point; the decision logic below only consumes these values.
205	type loginFlowFacts struct {
206		useDevice  bool // --device flag
207		canPrompt  bool // interactive terminal present
208		sshSession bool // running inside an SSH session
209	}
210	
211	// runLoginAuto picks between the browser (loopback authorization-code) and
212	// device-code flows and runs the chosen one. The browser flow is the
213	// default — no code to type, no poll latency — but it needs a browser that
214	// can reach this machine's 127.0.0.1, so headless terminals (CI, piped
215	// stdin), SSH sessions, and a loopback listener that fails to start all
216	// fall back to the device flow with a one-line explanation; the same
217	// both-flows-with-fallback shape gh / gcloud / aws sso ship. --device
218	// forces the device flow without commentary.
219	func runLoginAuto(ctx context.Context, outW, errW io.Writer, deviceClient deviceAuthClient, startBrowser func(context.Context) (browserAuthFlow, error), openURL browserOpenFunc, facts loginFlowFacts) error {
220		if shouldUseBrowserLogin(facts) {
221			flow, err := startBrowser(ctx)
222			if err != nil {
223				// Binding the loopback listener can fail (sandboxing, firewall,
224				// exhausted ports); that shouldn't strand the user — warn and
225				// use the device flow instead.
226				fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Warning: could not start browser sign-in (%v); falling back to the device-code flow.\n", err)
227				return runLogin(ctx, outW, errW, deviceClient, openURL, facts.canPrompt)
228			}
229			return runBrowserLogin(ctx, outW, errW, flow, deviceClient.BaseURL(), openURL, browserLoginTimeout)
230		}
231		switch {
232		case facts.useDevice:
233			// Explicitly requested; no explanation needed.
234		case !facts.canPrompt:
235			fmt.Fprintln(errW, "No interactive terminal detected; using device-code flow.")
236		case facts.sshSession:
237			fmt.Fprintln(errW, "SSH session detected; using device-code flow (a browser opened here couldn't reach this machine).")
238		}
239		return runLogin(ctx, outW, errW, deviceClient, openURL, facts.canPrompt)
240	}
241	
242	// shouldUseBrowserLogin reports whether `entire login` should use the
243	// loopback authorization-code (browser) flow. The browser flow is the
244	// default but needs a local browser + reachable 127.0.0.1, so it's only
245	// chosen when --device wasn't passed, an interactive terminal is present,
246	// and we're not inside an SSH session (where the loopback listener binds
247	// on the remote host, out of the user's browser's reach); otherwise the
248	// caller falls back to the device flow.
249	func shouldUseBrowserLogin(f loginFlowFacts) bool {
250		return !f.useDevice && f.canPrompt && !f.sshSession
251	}
252	
253	// isSSHSession reports whether this process is running inside an SSH
254	// session: sshd sets SSH_CONNECTION/SSH_CLIENT for every session and
255	// SSH_TTY for interactive ones.
256	func isSSHSession() bool {
257		return os.Getenv("SSH_CONNECTION") != "" ||
258			os.Getenv("SSH_CLIENT") != "" ||
259			os.Getenv("SSH_TTY") != ""
260	}
261	
262	// runBrowserLogin runs the loopback authorization-code flow on an
263	// already-started flow: open the authorization URL in the user's browser,
264	// wait up to waitTimeout for the redirect back to the local listener, then
265	// exchange the code for tokens. Shares the token validation + persistence
266	// tail with runLogin via persistLogin.
267	func runBrowserLogin(ctx context.Context, outW, errW io.Writer, flow browserAuthFlow, baseURL string, openURL browserOpenFunc, waitTimeout time.Duration) error {
268		// Wait tears the listener down on return, but Close is idempotent and
269		// covers the error paths before Wait runs.
270		defer func() { _ = flow.Close() }()
271	
272		// Mirror the device flow's interactive shape: show the URL, pause on
273		// Enter before opening the browser, then wait on the same line so
274		// persistLogin's "Login complete." reads "Waiting for sign-in...
275		// Login complete." runBrowserLogin is only reached interactively (see
276		// shouldUseBrowserLogin), so the Enter prompt is unconditional here.
277		authURL := flow.AuthorizationURL()
278		// Show the auth host, not the full authorize URL — the PKCE challenge +
279		// loopback redirect make it long and unreadable, and the browser is
280		// opened for the user anyway. The full URL is only printed below as a
281		// fallback when the browser can't be opened.
282		fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Logging in to: %s\n\n", baseURL)
283		fmt.Fprint(outW, "Press Enter to open in browser...")
284	
285		// Read from /dev/tty so we get a real keypress and don't consume piped stdin.
286		if err := waitForEnter(ctx); err != nil {
287			return fmt.Errorf("wait for input: %w", err)
288		}
289		fmt.Fprintln(outW)
290	
291		if err := openURL(ctx, authURL); err != nil {
292			fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Warning: failed to open browser: %v\n", err)
293			fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Open this URL in your browser to sign in: %s\n", authURL)
294		}
295	
296		fmt.Fprint(outW, "Waiting for sign-in... ")
297	
298		// The clock starts here, after the Enter prompt, so time spent reading
299		// the prompt isn't counted against the sign-in itself.
300		waitCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, waitTimeout)
301		defer cancel()
302	
303		code, err := flow.Wait(waitCtx)
304		if err != nil {
305			if errors.Is(waitCtx.Err(), context.DeadlineExceeded) {
306				return fmt.Errorf("timed out waiting for sign-in after %v; run `entire login` again, or use `entire login --device`", waitTimeout)
307			}
308			return fmt.Errorf("complete login: %w", err)
309		}
310	
311		token, refreshToken, err := flow.Exchange(ctx, code)
312		if err != nil {
313			return fmt.Errorf("complete login: %w", err)
314		}
315	
316		return persistLogin(outW, baseURL, token, refreshToken)
317	}
318	
319	// persistLogin validates the freshly-issued access token and records it in
320	// the shared contexts.json credential model. Shared by the device-code and
321	// browser flows.
322	func persistLogin(outW io.Writer, baseURL, token, refreshToken string) error {
323		if err := validateReceivedToken(token, baseURL, time.Now()); err != nil {
324			return fmt.Errorf("reject login token: %w", err)
325		}
326	
327		// Record the login in the shared contexts.json credential model — the
328		// single store every consumer (control plane, data API, git remote
329		// helper, entiredb's CLIs) resolves against.
330		if _, err := auth.RecordLoginContext(token, refreshToken, true); err != nil {
331			return fmt.Errorf("save login: %w", withHeadlessStoreHint(err))
332		}
333	
334		fmt.Fprintln(outW, "✓ Login complete.")
335		return nil
336	}
337	
338	// withHeadlessStoreHint appends file-token-store guidance to a credential
339	// store write failure. The default backend is the OS keyring, which locked
340	// or keyring-less machines (CI, containers, minimal server VMs) can't use —
341	// the raw store error gives those users no way forward (#1036). The hint is
342	// skipped when ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file is already set (suggesting it again
343	// would be nonsense) and for failures the file store wouldn't help with.
344	func withHeadlessStoreHint(err error) error {
345		if !errors.Is(err, auth.ErrCredentialStoreWrite) || tokenstore.FileBackendSelected() {
346			return err
347		}
348	
349		return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nIf this machine has no usable OS keyring (headless server, container, CI), store tokens in a file instead:\n\n  %s=file entire login\n\nTokens are then written with 0600 permissions to %s (override the location with %s)",
350			err, tokenstore.BackendEnvVar, tokenstore.FileBackendPath(), tokenstore.PathEnvVar)
351	}
352	
353	// validateReceivedToken runs minimum-trust checks on the access token
354	// the AS handed us before we persist it. The server is the authority
355	// on signature/exp; this is defense in depth aimed at catching gross
356	// misbehaviour by a compromised or misconfigured AS (e.g. handing back
357	// a token from a different issuer than the one we asked, or one whose
358	// claims are already-expired).
359	//
360	// It also enforces what the contexts model needs up front:
361	// RecordLoginContext — the sole persistence path — keys the context and
362	// keychain slot on the token's iss and handle/sub claims, so a token
363	// without parseable claims can never complete a login. Rejecting it here
364	// names the requirement instead of surfacing a parse error from the save
365	// step. Entire-core always issues claim-bearing JWTs; opaque-token-only
366	// servers are not supported.
367	func validateReceivedToken(rawToken, issuerURL string, now time.Time) error {
368		claims, err := tokens.ParseClaims(rawToken)
369		if errors.Is(err, tokens.ErrUnsignedJWT) {
370			return err //nolint:wrapcheck // sentinel surfaces verbatim for caller's errors.Is
371		}
372		if err != nil {
373			return fmt.Errorf("login server issued a token without parseable JWT claims (claim-bearing JWTs are required): %w", err)
374		}
375		if claims.Issuer == "" {
376			return errors.New("token has no iss claim; cannot record a login context")
377		}
378		if claims.Handle == "" && claims.Subject == "" {
379			return errors.New("token has no handle or sub claim; cannot record a login context")
380		}
381	
382		// iss check: the token must claim to come from the issuer we sent
383		// the device-code request to. A mismatch means either the AS is
384		// misconfigured or someone's playing games.
385		if issErr := issMatches(claims.Issuer, issuerURL); issErr != nil {
386			return issErr
387		}
388	
389		// exp sanity: a token that's already expired before we even store
390		// it is a smell. Don't reject if exp is unset (some servers omit).
391		if !claims.ExpiresAt.IsZero() && !now.Before(claims.ExpiresAt) {
392			return fmt.Errorf("token already expired (exp=%s, now=%s)",
393				claims.ExpiresAt.Format(time.RFC3339), now.Format(time.RFC3339))
394		}
395	
396		return nil
397	}
398	
399	// issMatches reports whether claimed equals expected after stripping path/
400	// query/fragment via api.OriginOnly, so "https://issuer/" and "https://issuer"
401	// match. The caller has already rejected an empty iss claim.
402	func issMatches(claimed, expected string) error {
403		normClaimed := api.OriginOnly(claimed)
404		normExpected := api.OriginOnly(expected)
405		if normClaimed != normExpected {
406			return fmt.Errorf("iss mismatch: token claims %q, expected %q", normClaimed, normExpected)
407		}
408		return nil
409	}
410	
411	func waitForApproval(ctx context.Context, poller deviceAuthClient, deviceCode string, expiresIn int, interval, slowDownBackoff time.Duration) (accessToken, refreshToken string, err error) {
412		expiry := time.Duration(expiresIn) * time.Second
413		if expiry <= 0 || expiry > maxExpiresIn {
414			expiry = maxExpiresIn
415		}
416		deadline := time.Now().Add(expiry)
417		pollInterval := interval
418		if pollInterval <= 0 {
419			pollInterval = fallbackDeviceAuthPollInterval
420		}
421	
422		consecutiveErrors := 0
423	
424		for {
425			if time.Now().After(deadline) {
426				return "", "", errors.New("device authorization expired")
427			}
428	
429			result, err := poller.PollDeviceAuth(ctx, deviceCode)
430			if err != nil {
431				consecutiveErrors++
432				if consecutiveErrors >= maxTransientErrors {
433					return "", "", fmt.Errorf("poll approval status (after %d consecutive failures): %w", consecutiveErrors, err)
434				}
435				// Transient error — wait and retry.
436				select {
437				case <-ctx.Done():
438					return "", "", fmt.Errorf("wait for approval: %w", ctx.Err())
439				case <-time.After(pollInterval):
440				}
441				continue
442			}
443			consecutiveErrors = 0
444	
445			switch result.Error {
446			case "":
447				if result.AccessToken == "" {
448					return "", "", errors.New("device authorization completed without a token")
449				}
450				return result.AccessToken, result.RefreshToken, nil
451			case "authorization_pending":
452				// no-op, will sleep and retry below
453			case "slow_down":
454				pollInterval += slowDownBackoff
455				if pollInterval > maxPollInterval {
456					pollInterval = maxPollInterval
457				}
458			case "access_denied":
459				return "", "", errors.New("device authorization denied")
460			case "expired_token":
461				return "", "", errors.New("device authorization expired")
462			default:
463				if result.ErrorDescription != "" {
464					return "", "", fmt.Errorf("device authorization failed: %s: %s", result.Error, result.ErrorDescription)
465				}
466				return "", "", fmt.Errorf("device authorization failed: %s", result.Error)
467			}
468	
469			select {
470			case <-ctx.Done():
471				return "", "", fmt.Errorf("wait for approval: %w", ctx.Err())
472			case <-time.After(pollInterval):
473			}
474		}
475	}
476	
477	// waitForEnter reads a line from /dev/tty, blocking until the user presses Enter.
478	// If /dev/tty cannot be opened (e.g. on Windows), it returns immediately.
479	// Returns ctx.Err() if the context is cancelled before the user presses Enter.
480	func waitForEnter(ctx context.Context) error {
481		// Under test (in-process go test, or a child with ENTIRE_TEST_TTY set)
482		// don't block on a real /dev/tty read — tests that force interactive
483		// mode still need this prompt to return. Mirrors openBrowser's guard.
484		if interactive.UnderTest() {
485			return nil
486		}
487	
488		tty, err := os.Open("/dev/tty")
489		if err != nil {
490			return nil //nolint:nilerr // tty unavailable (e.g. Windows) — skip prompt silently
491		}
492	
493		done := make(chan error, 1)
494		go func() {
495			reader := bufio.NewReader(tty)
496			_, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
497			done <- err
498		}()
499	
500		select {
501		case <-ctx.Done():
502			// Close tty to unblock the reading goroutine.
503			_ = tty.Close()
504			return fmt.Errorf("interrupted: %w", ctx.Err())
505		case <-done:
506			_ = tty.Close()
507			return nil
508		}
509	}
510	
511	func openBrowser(ctx context.Context, browserURL string) error {
512		u, err := url.Parse(browserURL)
513		if err != nil || (u.Scheme != schemeHTTPS && u.Scheme != schemeHTTP) {
514			return fmt.Errorf("refusing to open non-HTTP URL: %s", browserURL)
515		}
516	
517		// Under test there's no usable browser, and we must not spawn a real one
518		// on a dev/CI host. Report failure so the caller takes the "here's the
519		// URL" fallback — exactly the path a genuinely headless machine hits, and
520		// what lets an integration test recover the loopback callback URL from
521		// stdout. URL validation above still applies.
522		if interactive.UnderTest() {
523			return errors.New("browser unavailable under test")
524		}
525	
526		var command string
527		var args []string
528	
529		switch runtime.GOOS {
530		case "darwin":
531			command = "open"
532			args = []string{browserURL}
533		case "linux":
534			command = "xdg-open"
535			args = []string{browserURL}
536		case "windows":
537			command = "cmd"
538			args = []string{"/c", "start", "", browserURL}
539		default:
540			return fmt.Errorf("unsupported platform %s", runtime.GOOS)
541		}
542	
543		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, command, args...)
544		if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
545			return fmt.Errorf("start browser command %q: %w", command, err)
546		}
547	
548		if err := cmd.Process.Release(); err != nil {
549			return fmt.Errorf("release browser process: %w", err)
550		}
551	
552		return nil
553	}

17	)

19	// envKillSwitch disables the interactive update prompt regardless of TTY.
20	const envKillSwitch = "ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE"
21	
22	// AutoUpdateAction describes the result of an update prompt.
23	type AutoUpdateAction string
24	
25	const (
26		autoUpdateActionSkip                 AutoUpdateAction = "skip"
27		autoUpdateActionUpdate               AutoUpdateAction = "update"
28		autoUpdateActionSkipUntilNextVersion AutoUpdateAction = "skip_until_next_version"
29	)
30	
31	// chooseUpdateFn is the signature for the update-prompt seam. The
32	// concrete implementation renders a huh.Select with the installer
33	// command interpolated into option 1.
34	type chooseUpdateFn func(ctx context.Context, currentVersion, latestVersion, cmdStr string) (AutoUpdateAction, error)
35	
36	// Test seams.
37	var (
38		runInstaller                 = realRunInstaller
39		chooseUpdate  chooseUpdateFn = realChooseUpdate
40		isTerminalOut                = interactive.IsTerminalWriter
41	)
42	
43	// MaybeAutoUpdate prints an update notification and offers an interactive
44	// upgrade. Silent on every failure path — it must never interrupt the CLI.
45	//
46	// The same 3-option prompt (update / skip / skip until next version) is
47	// shown for every install manager that supports auto-installation
48	// (brew, mise, scoop, curl-bash). The only thing that varies between
49	// installers is the shell command interpolated into option 1.
50	//
51	// If the installer command fails, a hint with the exact command is
52	// printed so the user can retry manually. The 24h version-check cache
53	// is not invalidated on failure: we don't want to re-prompt on every
54	// invocation while an upstream issue (network, auth, repo outage) is
55	// still in place.
56	//
57	// When the prompt cannot be shown (kill switch set, or non-interactive
58	// environment like CI / agent subprocess / no TTY) the installer
59	// command is printed so the user still learns what to run manually.
60	//
61	// On Windows + unknown install manager the POSIX curl-pipe-bash fallback
62	// can't auto-run and there's no native equivalent, so we point the user
63	// at the releases download page instead.
64	func MaybeAutoUpdate(ctx context.Context, w io.Writer, currentVersion, latestVersion string) AutoUpdateAction {
65		if !canAutoInstall() {
66			printNotification(w, currentVersion, latestVersion)
67			fmt.Fprintf(w, "To update, download the latest release from:\n  %s\n", downloadsURL)
68			return autoUpdateActionSkip
69		}
70	
71		cmdStr := updateCommand(currentVersion)
72	
73		if os.Getenv(envKillSwitch) != "" || !interactive.CanPromptInteractively() || !isTerminalOut(w) {
74			printNotification(w, currentVersion, latestVersion)
75			fmt.Fprintf(w, "To update, run:\n  %s\n", cmdStr)
76			return autoUpdateActionSkip
77		}
78	
79		action, err := chooseUpdate(ctx, currentVersion, latestVersion, cmdStr)
80		if err != nil {
81			logging.Debug(ctx, "auto-update: prompt failed", "error", err.Error())
82			return autoUpdateActionSkip
83		}
84	
85		switch action {
86		case autoUpdateActionUpdate:
87			fmt.Fprintf(w, "\nUpdating Entire CLI: %s\n", cmdStr)
88			if err := runInstaller(ctx, cmdStr); err != nil {
89				fmt.Fprintf(w, "Update failed: %v\nTry again later running:\n  %s\n", err, cmdStr)
90				return autoUpdateActionUpdate
91			}
92			fmt.Fprintln(w, "Update complete. Re-run entire to use the new version.")
93			return autoUpdateActionUpdate
94		case autoUpdateActionSkipUntilNextVersion:
95			return autoUpdateActionSkipUntilNextVersion
96		case autoUpdateActionSkip:
97			return autoUpdateActionSkip
98		default:
99			return autoUpdateActionSkip
100		}
101	}
102	
103	// realChooseUpdate renders a huh.Select with the three update actions.
104	// In normal mode this is an arrow-key TUI; when ACCESSIBLE is set huh
105	// falls back to a plain numbered prompt readable by screen readers.
106	func realChooseUpdate(ctx context.Context, currentVersion, latestVersion, cmdStr string) (AutoUpdateAction, error) {
107		action := autoUpdateActionUpdate
108		sel := huh.NewSelect[AutoUpdateAction]().
109			Title(fmt.Sprintf("Update available! %s -> %s",
110				displayVersion(currentVersion), displayVersion(latestVersion))).
111			Description("Release notes: "+releaseNotesURL(latestVersion)).
112			Options(
113				huh.NewOption(fmt.Sprintf("Update now (runs `%s`)", cmdStr), autoUpdateActionUpdate),
114				huh.NewOption("Skip", autoUpdateActionSkip),
115				huh.NewOption("Skip until next version", autoUpdateActionSkipUntilNextVersion),
116			).
117			Value(&action)
118		form := uiform.New(huh.NewGroup(sel))
119		if err := form.RunWithContext(ctx); err != nil {
120			if errors.Is(err, huh.ErrUserAborted) || errors.Is(err, huh.ErrTimeout) {
121				return autoUpdateActionSkip, nil
122			}
123			return autoUpdateActionSkip, fmt.Errorf("update prompt: %w", err)
124		}
125		return action, nil
126	}
127	
128	// realRunInstaller shells out to the installer command, streaming stdin/stdout/stderr
129	// so password prompts and progress output reach the user.
130	func realRunInstaller(ctx context.Context, cmdStr string) error {
131		var c *exec.Cmd
132		if runtime.GOOS == goosWindows {
133			c = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "cmd", "/C", cmdStr)
134		} else {
135			c = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", cmdStr)
136		}
137		c.Stdin = os.Stdin
138		c.Stdout = os.Stdout
139		c.Stderr = os.Stderr
140		if err := c.Run(); err != nil {
141			return fmt.Errorf("installer exited: %w", err)
142		}
143		return nil
144	}

3	import (

17	)
18	
19	// defaultSavedTokenTTL is the encoded keychain expiry used when a refreshed
20	// token carries no usable ExpiresAt. The server is the real authority; this
21	// only governs when local readers consider the cached token stale.
22	const defaultSavedTokenTTL = time.Hour
23	
24	// contextTokenStore adapts one login context's keyring slots to auth-go's
25	// tokenstore.Store, so tokenmanager can load, refresh, and persist that
26	// context's credentials. It is bound to a specific (service, handle) at
27	// construction and ignores the profile argument: the cluster resolver has
28	// already chosen exactly one context, so there is no per-issuer account
29	// ambiguity to resolve here.
30	//
31	// Access token lives at `service`/`handle` (with the "|<expiry>" encoding
32	// the rest of the CLI reads); the refresh token lives raw at
33	// `service:refresh`/`handle`.
34	type contextTokenStore struct {
35		service string
36		handle  string
37	}
38	
39	func (s contextTokenStore) LoadTokens(string) (tokens.TokenSet, error) {
40		enc, err := tokenstore.Get(s.service, s.handle)
41		// Map "no credential stored" to auth-go's sentinel so tokenmanager
42		// reports "not logged in" rather than a hard store failure.
43		if errors.Is(err, tokenstore.ErrNotFound) || (err == nil && enc == "") {
44			return tokens.TokenSet{}, authtokenstore.ErrNotFound
45		}
46		if err != nil {
47			return tokens.TokenSet{}, fmt.Errorf("read access token: %w", err)
48		}
49		access, expiresAt := tokenstore.DecodeTokenWithExpiration(enc)
50		// A missing refresh slot is fine (login predating offline_access) — treat
51		// it as no-refresh. Any other store error must surface, not be swallowed:
52		// dropping it would silently discard a valid refresh token and force a
53		// re-login on what was really a transient keyring/file-store failure.
54		refresh, err := tokenstore.Get(tokenstore.RefreshService(s.service), s.handle)
55		if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, tokenstore.ErrNotFound) {
56			return tokens.TokenSet{}, fmt.Errorf("read refresh token: %w", err)
57		}
58		return tokens.TokenSet{
59			AccessToken:  access,
60			RefreshToken: refresh,
61			ExpiresAt:    expiresAt,
62		}, nil
63	}
64	
65	func (s contextTokenStore) SaveTokens(_ string, t tokens.TokenSet) error {
66		if t.AccessToken == "" {
67			return errors.New("save tokens: empty access token")
68		}
69		expiresIn := int64(defaultSavedTokenTTL.Seconds())
70		if !t.ExpiresAt.IsZero() {
71			if secs := int64(time.Until(t.ExpiresAt).Seconds()); secs > 0 {
72				expiresIn = secs
73			}
74		}
75		// Persist the rotated refresh token BEFORE the access token. The server
76		// single-use-rotates refresh tokens, so a partial write must never leave
77		// a fresh access token paired with a stale refresh token: that pairing
78		// looks healthy until the access token expires, then the dead refresh
79		// token trips invalid_grant/family revocation and forces a re-login.
80		// Refresh-first inverts the failure modes: a failed refresh write aborts
81		// before touching the access slot (old pair preserved), and a failed
82		// access write after a good refresh write self-heals on the next load
83		// (the new refresh token re-mints an access token).
84		//
85		// persistRefreshed carries a still-valid refresh token forward when the
86		// server doesn't rotate, so an empty value here means "leave as-is",
87		// never "clear".
88		if t.RefreshToken != "" {
89			if err := tokenstore.Set(tokenstore.RefreshService(s.service), s.handle, t.RefreshToken); err != nil {
90				return fmt.Errorf("store refresh token: %w", err)
91			}
92		}
93		if err := tokenstore.Set(s.service, s.handle, tokenstore.EncodeTokenWithExpiration(t.AccessToken, expiresIn)); err != nil {
94			return fmt.Errorf("store access token: %w", err)
95		}
96		return nil
97	}
98	
99	func (s contextTokenStore) DeleteTokens(string) error {
100		_ = tokenstore.Delete(tokenstore.RefreshService(s.service), s.handle) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort; the access-token delete below is what matters
101		if err := tokenstore.Delete(s.service, s.handle); err != nil {
102			return fmt.Errorf("delete access token: %w", err)
103		}
104		return nil
105	}
106	
107	// newContextTokenManager builds the per-context auth-go tokenmanager that both
108	// NewRefreshingLoginProvider and NewRefreshingResourceProvider sit on. Keying
109	// Issuer on c.CoreURL is the whole point: store reads, the refresh grant, and
110	// the STS exchange all target that context's core, so a multi-core user's
111	// credentials never travel to (or get keyed under) a host the context
112	// doesn't belong to.
113	//
114	// transport carries the caller's TLS configuration; allowInsecureHTTP permits
115	// an http:// core/resource for loopback/dev.
116	func newContextTokenManager(c *contexts.Context, transport http.RoundTripper, allowInsecureHTTP bool) (*tokenmanager.Manager, error) {
117		if c == nil {
118			return nil, errors.New("nil context")
119		}
120		if c.KeychainService == "" || c.Handle == "" {
121			return nil, fmt.Errorf("context %q has no keychain slot", c.Name)
122		}
123		mgr, err := tokenmanager.New(tokenmanager.Config{
124			Issuer:            strings.TrimRight(c.CoreURL, "/"),
125			ClientID:          oauthClientID,
126			STSPath:           oauthSTSPath,
127			RefreshPath:       oauthTokenPath,
128			Store:             contextTokenStore{service: c.KeychainService, handle: c.Handle},
129			Transport:         transport,
130			AllowInsecureHTTP: allowInsecureHTTP,
131			UserAgent:         oauthClientID,
132		})
133		if err != nil {
134			return nil, fmt.Errorf("init token manager for context %q: %w", c.Name, err)
135		}
136		return mgr, nil
137	}
138	
139	// reauthError carries a friendly, context-named re-login message while still
140	// unwrapping to the underlying tokenmanager sentinel, so callers that branch
141	// on errors.Is(err, ErrNotLoggedIn) (NewAuthenticatedAPIClient, search,
142	// dispatch) keep matching. Error() returns only msg so the sentinel's terse
143	// text ("not logged in") doesn't leak into the rendered message.
144	type reauthError struct {
145		msg      string
146		sentinel error
147	}
148	
149	func (e *reauthError) Error() string { return e.msg }
150	func (e *reauthError) Unwrap() error { return e.sentinel }
151	
152	// contextReauthError maps the two re-auth sentinels a per-context manager can
153	// return into a friendly message that names the context and its core (so a
154	// multi-core user logs back into the right one — matching the
155	// "no auth context, run `entire login`" hint style used by clusterdiscovery),
156	// preserving the sentinel for errors.Is. Returns nil when err is neither
157	// sentinel, leaving the caller to wrap the residual error in its own terms
158	// (refresh vs exchange).
159	func contextReauthError(c *contexts.Context, err error) error {
160		coreURL := strings.TrimRight(c.CoreURL, "/")
161		switch {
162		case errors.Is(err, tokenmanager.ErrReauthRequired):
163			return &reauthError{
164				msg:      fmt.Sprintf("login session for %q (%s) expired; run `entire login` to re-authenticate", c.Name, coreURL),
165				sentinel: tokenmanager.ErrReauthRequired,
166			}
167		case errors.Is(err, tokenmanager.ErrNotLoggedIn):
168			return &reauthError{
169				msg:      fmt.Sprintf("no usable login for %q (%s); run `entire login`", c.Name, coreURL),
170				sentinel: tokenmanager.ErrNotLoggedIn,
171			}
172		}
173		return nil
174	}
175	
176	// NewRefreshingLoginProvider returns a login-JWT provider (the shape
177	// repocreds wants) for context c that transparently re-mints an expired
178	// login JWT from the stored refresh token.
179	//
180	// It is backed by auth-go's tokenmanager, which is what makes this safe
181	// against the server's single-use refresh-token rotation: refreshes are
182	// serialised across processes (an advisory file lock) and goroutines, the
183	// store is re-read after locking so a late waiter reuses a peer's freshly
184	// minted token, and the rotated refresh token is persisted. Without that,
185	// two concurrent git-remote-entire processes (e.g. a recursive submodule
186	// fetch) could replay the same single-use token and trip the server's
187	// reuse detection, revoking the whole family.
188	//
189	// A still-valid token is returned with no network call. A context with no
190	// stored refresh token degrades gracefully: valid token used, expired token
191	// surfaces a re-login error.
192	//
193	// transport carries the caller's TLS configuration; allowInsecureHTTP
194	// permits an http:// core for loopback/dev.
195	func NewRefreshingLoginProvider(c *contexts.Context, transport http.RoundTripper, allowInsecureHTTP bool) (func(context.Context) (string, error), error) {
196		mgr, err := newContextTokenManager(c, transport, allowInsecureHTTP)
197		if err != nil {
198			return nil, err
199		}
200		return func(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
201			tok, err := mgr.Refresh(ctx)
202			if mapped := contextReauthError(c, err); mapped != nil {
203				return "", mapped
204			}
205			if err != nil {
206				return "", fmt.Errorf("refresh login token: %w", err)
207			}
208			return tok, nil
209		}, nil
210	}
211	
212	// RefreshedLoginToken returns context c's login JWT, transparently re-minting
213	// an expired one from the stored refresh token. It is the convenience form of
214	// NewRefreshingLoginProvider for callers that want a single token now (e.g.
215	// `auth status` / `logout`, which must report a refreshable session as alive
216	// rather than telling the user to re-login). The insecure-HTTP decision mirrors
217	// the control-plane resolver: loopback cores and the --insecure-http-auth
218	// opt-in are permitted, everything else requires https.
219	//
220	// Errors preserve the tokenmanager sentinels (ErrReauthRequired when the
221	// session is genuinely dead, ErrNotLoggedIn when no credential is usable) so
222	// callers can branch on errors.Is.
223	func RefreshedLoginToken(ctx context.Context, c *contexts.Context) (string, error) {
224		if c == nil {
225			return "", errors.New("nil context")
226		}
227		provider, err := NewRefreshingLoginProvider(c, nil, insecureHTTPEnabled() || isLoopbackHTTP(c.CoreURL))
228		if err != nil {
229			return "", err
230		}
231		return provider(ctx)
232	}
233	
234	// NewRefreshingResourceProvider returns a provider that mints a bearer valid
235	// for resourceOrigin, by exchanging context c's login JWT at c's own core (RFC
236	// 8693). It is NewRefreshingLoginProvider's sibling for resource servers: where
237	// that returns the bare login JWT (the control plane / cluster cases, where the
238	// host is the core), this performs the token exchange the data API requires.
239	//
240	// Both the silent login-JWT re-mint and the exchange run through the shared
241	// per-context tokenmanager (newContextTokenManager). resourceOrigin must
242	// already be origin-only (no path). No audience is passed: the token manager
243	// defaults the RFC 8693 audience to the resource origin, which is exactly what
244	// the data API requires (aud == its base URI), so the audience is derived from
245	// the host being dialed rather than read from discovery. Exchanged tokens are
246	// cached in-process by the tokenmanager for the life of this process.
247	//
248	// transport carries the caller's TLS configuration; allowInsecureHTTP permits
249	// an http:// core/resource for loopback/dev.
250	func NewRefreshingResourceProvider(c *contexts.Context, resourceOrigin string, transport http.RoundTripper, allowInsecureHTTP bool) (func(context.Context) (string, error), error) {
251		mgr, err := newContextTokenManager(c, transport, allowInsecureHTTP)
252		if err != nil {
253			return nil, err
254		}
255		req := tokenmanager.TokenRequest{Resource: resourceOrigin}
256		return func(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
257			tok, err := mgr.Token(ctx, req)
258			if mapped := contextReauthError(c, err); mapped != nil {
259				return "", mapped
260			}
261			if err != nil {
262				return "", fmt.Errorf("exchange token for %s: %w", resourceOrigin, err)
263			}
264			return tok, nil
265		}, nil
266	}

1	package httputil
2	
3	import (
4		"bytes"
5		"context"
6		"encoding/json"
7		"errors"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"

11		"net/url"
12		"strings"
13	)
14	
15	// RFC 8693 grant + token-type URNs. Re-export the literals so callers
16	// composing /oauth/token forms don't keep parallel copies. Lifted out
17	// of core/repoadmin and core/api during COR-337 cleanup.
18	const (
19		GrantTypeTokenExchange = "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange" //nolint:gosec // G101: an OAuth grant_type URN, not a credential
20		TokenTypeAccessToken   = "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token"   //nolint:gosec // G101: an RFC 8693 token-type URN, not a credential
21	)
22	
23	// OAuthClientID is the public OAuth client_id the CLI identifies as on
24	// /oauth/token. Lifted into Basic auth by PostOAuthToken.
25	const OAuthClientID = "entire-cli"
26	
27	// TokenExchangeForm builds the RFC 8693 token-exchange form every CLI
28	// exchange POSTs to /oauth/token: subjectToken (the login JWT) is traded
29	// for an access token pinned to audience with the given scope. The one
30	// form shape serves repo-scoped and jurisdiction tokens alike — only
31	// audience and scope differ — so keep call sites on this builder rather
32	// than open-coding the fields.
33	func TokenExchangeForm(subjectToken, audience, scope string) url.Values {
34		form := url.Values{}
35		form.Set("grant_type", GrantTypeTokenExchange)
36		form.Set("subject_token_type", TokenTypeAccessToken)
37		form.Set("subject_token", subjectToken)
38		form.Set("requested_token_type", TokenTypeAccessToken)
39		form.Set("audience", audience)
40		form.Set("scope", scope)
41		form.Set("client_id", OAuthClientID)
42		return form
43	}
44	
45	// BufferRequestBody reads the request body once so a fallback retry
46	// can replay it. http.NoBody (and nil) short-circuits — both signal
47	// "no body" but only the latter is a runtime nil, so the explicit
48	// identity check keeps the cloned request's Content-Length correct on
49	// the wire. Returns (nil, nil) for no-body requests; the caller can
50	// safely forward without replay state.
51	func BufferRequestBody(req *http.Request) ([]byte, error) {
52		if req.Body == nil || req.Body == http.NoBody {
53			return nil, nil
54		}
55		b, err := io.ReadAll(req.Body)
56		_ = req.Body.Close()
57		if err != nil {
58			return nil, fmt.Errorf("buffer request body: %w", err)
59		}
60		return b, nil
61	}
62	
63	// BodyReader wraps a buffered request body so http.Request.Body /
64	// GetBody can replay it across a retry. Pair with BufferRequestBody.
65	func BodyReader(body []byte) io.ReadCloser {
66		return io.NopCloser(bytes.NewReader(body))
67	}
68	
69	// cloneValuesWithoutClient returns a shallow copy of v with the
70	// client_id and client_secret keys removed. Used so we can lift them
71	// into Basic auth without mutating the caller's form.
72	func cloneValuesWithoutClient(v url.Values) url.Values {
73		out := make(url.Values, len(v))
74		for k, vs := range v {
75			if k == "client_id" || k == "client_secret" {
76				continue
77			}
78			out[k] = vs
79		}
80		return out
81	}
82	
83	// OAuthError is returned by PostOAuthToken when the OAuth endpoint
84	// responds with a non-200 status. Callers can errors.As it to surface
85	// status-specific UX (e.g. a friendly 403 message) or branch on the
86	// RFC 6749 error code.
87	type OAuthError struct {
88		Status      int
89		Code        string // RFC 6749 `error` code from the response body; "" when not present
90		Description string // RFC 6749 `error_description` from the response body; "" when not present
91		Body        string
92	}
93	
94	func (e *OAuthError) Error() string {
95		return fmt.Sprintf("HTTP %d: %s", e.Status, e.Body)
96	}
97	
98	// PostOAuthToken posts a form-encoded request to coreURL+"/oauth/token"
99	// and parses the standard {access_token, expires_in} response. Callers
100	// build the form (grant_type, subject_token, audience, etc.) so the
101	// helper stays neutral about which OAuth grant is being exercised.
102	//
103	// If the form carries client_id (and optionally client_secret), the
104	// helper lifts both into an HTTP Basic Authorization header and drops
105	// them from the form body. zitadel/oidc's token endpoint reads client
106	// credentials only from Basic auth, so form-only client_id produces
107	// invalid_client even when the form is otherwise well-formed. Both values
108	// are url.QueryEscaped per RFC 6749 §2.3.1 because pkg/op QueryUnescapes
109	// them on the other side — a raw '+'/'%xx' would round-trip to a different
110	// value and fail invalid_client (matches core/api/token_endpoint.go).
111	//
112	// coreURL must already be trimmed of any trailing slash. A non-200
113	// response is surfaced as *OAuthError (RFC 6749 defines token-endpoint
114	// success as 200 only); transport and decode failures
115	// are wrapped plain errors.
116	func PostOAuthToken(ctx context.Context, httpClient *http.Client, coreURL string, form url.Values) (accessToken string, expiresIn int, err error) {
117		clientID := form.Get("client_id")
118		clientSecret := form.Get("client_secret")
119		if clientID != "" {
120			form = cloneValuesWithoutClient(form)
121		}
122	
123		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost,
124			coreURL+"/oauth/token", strings.NewReader(form.Encode()))
125		if err != nil {
126			return "", 0, fmt.Errorf("build token request: %w", err)
127		}
128		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
129		if clientID != "" {
130			// RFC 6749 §2.3.1: percent-encode before Basic so pkg/op's

Assessment first — no code change yet.

**Should login catch it?** Yes, but not as only place. Login is where user ends up ("run `entire login`"), so hint there is necessary — but my current wrap at login `RunE` is too narrow.

**Where else can it happen?** Structurally, everywhere the CLI talks to auth-server OAuth endpoints. auth-go surfaces the same `oauth error: cli_upgrade_required` string from all four flows (`deviceflow`, `authcode`, `refresh`, `sts` — all use shared `oauthhttp.ReadOAuthError`). CLI entry points:

| Path | Trigger | User sees hint today? |
|---|---|---|
| Device/browser login | `entire login` | Yes (my fix) |
| Refresh grant (`auth/refresh.go` providers) | Nearly every authenticated command — `api`, `org/project/repo`, `activity`, `search`, `auth status` — once cached token expires | No |
| STS exchange (`tokenmanager.Token`, `exchange.go`) | `auth token --jurisdiction`, `api --to cell`, experts, cell fan-out | No |
| `httputil.PostOAuthToken` callers | `repocreds`, `cross_juris_transport`, `api/base_url.go` | No |
| `git-remote-entire` (separate binary, `jurisdictionauth.go`) | git fetch/push via helper | No |

Whether the server actually gates refresh/STS today unknown from client side — but already-logged-in user with old CLI hitting a min-version bump at refresh time is the likely next report.

**Right place:** `cmd/entire/main.go:126` — the default error-print arm. Repo's error architecture already funnels every non-`SilentError` command error there (root sets `SilenceErrors`, main prints). One `withCLIUpgradeHint(err)` there covers login, refresh, exchange, every command — and login `RunE` wrap becomes redundant, delete it. Helper stays exported in `cli` package.

Known gaps with that choke point, both acceptable:
- `SilentError` paths bypass it — but those print curated messages, not raw oauth codes.
- `git-remote-entire` has own main; needs same one-liner at its error exit if server ever gates repo-creds exchange. Separate small follow-up.

Want me to move the hint to `main.go` and drop the login-local wrap?

input.command:
gh pr create --title "fix: hint CLI update command on cli_upgrade_required errors" --body "## Problem

\`entire login\` against a server that requires a newer CLI failed with only the raw OAuth code:

\`\`\`
start login: start device auth: cli_upgrade_required
\`\`\`

No way forward for the user — while the periodic version check (plain \`entire\`) does show the update command.

## Fix

Append the install-manager-aware update command (from \`versioncheck.UpdateCommandForCurrentBinary\`, the same one the version check advertises) whenever a command error carries \`cli_upgrade_required\`:

\`\`\`
start login: start device auth: oauth error: cli_upgrade_required

This version of the Entire CLI is too old for this server. Update it, then rerun the command:

  curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
\`\`\`

## Why main.go, not login

The code can surface from any auth-server OAuth flow — auth-go emits the same error string from \`deviceflow\`, \`authcode\`, \`refresh\`, and \`sts\`. That means not just login, but the refresh grant under nearly every authenticated command and the RFC 8693 exchanges (jurisdiction/cell tokens). \`main.go\`'s default error-print arm is the repo's documented single choke point for command errors (root sets \`SilenceErrors\`, main prints), so one \`cli.WithCLIUpgradeHint(err)\` there covers all of them.

Detection is a string match on the code — auth-go exposes no sentinel for unrecognised OAuth codes.

Known gaps (accepted): \`SilentError\` paths bypass the printer (they print curated messages, not raw OAuth codes); \`git-remote-entire\` is a separate binary and would need the same one-liner if the server ever gates repo-creds exchange.

## Testing

- Unit tests for \`WithCLIUpgradeHint\` (login-shaped and refresh-shaped errors, pass-through, nil)
- \`mise run test:ci\` green (unit + integration + e2e canary)
- Verified end-to-end: real binary against a fake AS returning \`cli_upgrade_required\` prints the hint above

content.text:
No. Only `update` hits are `trail update` subcommands — unrelated.

Upgrade today has two paths, no dedicated command:
1. **Interactive prompt** — `versioncheck.MaybeAutoUpdate` fires after any command (24h cache, TTY only), offers "Update now" and runs installer itself.
2. **Manual command** — brew/mise/scoop/curl string from `updateCommand()`, printed in notifications and now in the `cli_upgrade_required` hint.

Worth noting: all machinery for `entire upgrade` already exists — `updateCommand()` picks the right installer, `realRunInstaller()` executes it streaming output. A thin cobra command wrapping those would be ~30 lines. Then the hint could say `run: entire upgrade` instead of raw curl — nicer, and stable across install managers.

Want that as follow-up PR? (Separate concern, separate PR per your isolated-PRs preference.)

gh pr edit 1794 --body "## Problem

Any command hitting a server that requires a newer CLI failed with only the raw OAuth code:

\`\`\`
start login: start device auth: cli_upgrade_required
\`\`\`

No way forward for the user — while the periodic version check (plain \`entire\`) does show the update command.

## Fix

Handle \`cli_upgrade_required\` at \`main.go\`'s central error-print arm (\`cli.OfferCLIUpgradeIfRequired\`):

**Interactive terminal** — offer the update right away (Yes/No confirm, accessible-form aware), running the same installer the version-check prompt uses. Honors \`ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE\` and platforms without a runnable installer (Windows + unknown manager falls back to print).

**Non-interactive (or declined/aborted)** — print the update command and the failed command, ready to copy:

\`\`\`
start login: start device auth: oauth error: cli_upgrade_required

This Entire CLI version is no longer supported. Update it, then rerun the command:

  curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
  entire login --device
\`\`\`

## Why main.go, not login

The code can surface from any auth-server OAuth flow — auth-go emits the same error string from \`deviceflow\`, \`authcode\`, \`refresh\`, and \`sts\`. That means not just login, but the refresh grant under nearly every authenticated command and the RFC 8693 exchanges (jurisdiction/cell tokens). \`main.go\`'s default error-print arm is the repo's documented single choke point for command errors, so one handler there covers all of them.

Detection is a string match on the code — auth-go exposes no sentinel for unrecognised OAuth codes.

Known gaps (accepted): \`SilentError\` paths bypass the printer (they print curated messages, not raw OAuth codes); \`git-remote-entire\` is a separate binary and would need the same one-liner if the server ever gates repo-creds exchange.

## Testing

- Unit tests for \`IsCLIUpgradeRequired\`, both prompt branches (Yes runs installer, No prints commands), installer failure, non-interactive print, and argv reconstruction (injected deps, fully parallel)
- \`mise run test:ci\` green (one unrelated flake, \`TestIsMetadataDisconnected_NoLocal\` in strategy, passes 4/4 in isolation and full-package rerun)
- Verified end-to-end: real binary against a fake AS returning \`cli_upgrade_required\` prints the block above

input.description: Read current PR body

content.content:
## Problem

Any command hitting a server that requires a newer CLI failed with only the raw OAuth code:

```
start login: start device auth: cli_upgrade_required
```

No way forward for the user — while the periodic version check (plain `entire`) does show the update command.

## Fix

Handle `cli_upgrade_required` at `main.go`'s central error-print arm (`cli.OfferCLIUpgradeIfRequired`):

**Interactive terminal** — offer the update right away (Yes/No confirm, accessible-form aware), running the same installer the version-check prompt uses. Honors `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE` and platforms without a runnable installer (Windows + unknown manager falls back to print).

**Non-interactive (or declined/aborted)** — print the update command and the failed command, ready to copy (the raw OAuth error chain is suppressed — the guidance says everything it did; exit code stays 1):

```
This Entire CLI version is no longer supported. Update it:

  curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash

Then rerun the command:

  entire login --device
```

## Why main.go, not login

The code can surface from any auth-server OAuth flow — auth-go emits the same error string from `deviceflow`, `authcode`, `refresh`, and `sts`. That means not just login, but the refresh grant under nearly every authenticated command and the RFC 8693 exchanges (jurisdiction/cell tokens). `main.go`'s default error-print arm is the repo's documented single choke point for command errors, so one handler there covers all of them.

Detection is a string match on the code — auth-go exposes no sentinel for unrecognised OAuth codes.

Known gaps (accepted): `SilentError` paths bypass the printer (they print curated messages, not raw OAuth codes); `git-remote-entire` is a separate binary and would need the same one-liner if the server ever gates repo-creds exchange.

## Testing

- Unit tests for `IsCLIUpgradeRequired`, both prompt branches (Yes runs installer, No prints commands), installer failure, non-interactive print, and argv reconstruction (injected deps, fully parallel)
- `mise run test:ci` green (one unrelated flake, `TestIsMetadataDisconnected_NoLocal` in strategy, passes 4/4 in isolation and full-package rerun)
- Verified end-to-end: real binary against a fake AS returning `cli_upgrade_required` prints the block above

Base directory for this skill: /Users/gtrrz-victor/.claude/skills/review-pr-feedback

# Review PR Feedback

Walk every unresolved review thread on the PR for the current branch. For each
thread, decide whether it's actionable, fixable, or needs the user's input.
Apply fixes, post a reply explaining what changed, and resolve the thread.

## Step 1: Locate the PR

1. If `` is a number, use that PR.
2. Otherwise resolve from the current branch:
   ```
   gh pr view --json number,url
   ```
3. If there is no PR for the current branch, stop and tell the user.

## Step 2: List every review thread (resolved status + bodies)

GitHub's REST endpoints don't expose `isResolved`, so use GraphQL:

```
gh api graphql -f query='query {
  repository(owner:"<OWNER>", name:"<REPO>") {
    pullRequest(number:<NUM>) {
      reviewThreads(first:100) {
        nodes {
          id isResolved isOutdated path line
          comments(first:20) {
            nodes { databaseId author { login } body createdAt }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}'
```

Also pull issue-level comments for context:

```
gh api repos/<OWNER>/<REPO>/issues/<NUM>/comments
```

Save the GraphQL result so you can reference thread IDs and the first
comment's `databaseId` (used as the reply parent below).

## Step 3: Triage and group threads

For each thread that is **not** already `isResolved`:

- Read the body fully — bot comments (Cursor Bugbot, Copilot, etc.) are often
  long and the actionable bit is buried after metadata.
- Classify as one of:
  - **Easy fix** — uncontroversial, narrow scope (e.g. "use `f.Reader` instead
    of `f.Contents`", "add validation", "fix typo"). Just do it.
  - **Already fixed** — earlier commits on the branch already addressed the
    concern. Don't re-fix; reply explaining where it landed.
  - **Outdated/no longer applies** — code shape changed. Reply briefly noting
    the current state and resolve.
  - **Needs decision** — design tradeoff, scope question, or "won't fix"
    candidate. Hold for the user.
- For threads marked `isOutdated`: still address them; outdated ≠ irrelevant,
  GitHub just collapsed them because the underlying line moved.

Skip resolved threads silently — those have already been handled.

## Step 4: Ask the user about the hard ones

Before applying any fixes that involve a tradeoff or non-trivial scope, batch
the open questions into a single `AskUserQuestion` call. Group easy-fix
threads as one question ("OK to apply these N small fixes and resolve?"
with options for "do all", "do some", "skip"). Keep questions short and
include enough context that the user doesn't have to scroll back.

If a thread reports a security or correctness concern that needs a real
investigation (e.g. "race condition under concurrent X"), surface that
explicitly rather than treating it as easy.

## Step 5: Apply fixes

Make the code changes, then run before pushing:

```
go build ./...   # or the project's build command
mise run fmt
mise run lint
mise run test    # or test:ci, depending on scope
```

Fix any linter/test fallout from the changes. Don't push if anything is red.

If a `nolint` directive becomes "unused" after a config change, decide
between adding the type to the linter allowlist (preferred for stable cases)
or removing the directive — never both.

## Step 6: Commit and push

Stage only the files you changed (never `git add -A`). Use one commit per
logical group; e.g. one for the "easy fixes" batch, one per substantial
change. Commit messages focus on **why**, not **what**. Reference PR
threads by topic, not by GitHub numeric ID — those don't render anywhere
useful.

Push:

```
git push
```

## Step 7: Reply on each thread + resolve

Use the **first comment's `databaseId`** as the parent, not the thread ID:

```
# Reply

  resolveReviewThread(input: {threadId: $id}) {

  }
}' -F id="<THREAD_ID>"
```

- Cite the commit hash that addressed the concern: `Fixed in abc1234.`
- Summarize **what** changed in one sentence — the reviewer doesn't need a
  detailed explanation, just enough to verify.
- For "won't fix" replies, give the rationale once, briefly. Don't argue.

## Step 8: Final sweep

After resolving everything you can, re-run the GraphQL query to confirm:

```
gh api graphql -f query='query { ... reviewThreads { nodes { id isResolved } } }'
```

Report to the user:
- Number of threads addressed (with one-line summary each)
- Number deferred and why
- Final commit hash + PR URL

## Rules

- Never resolve a thread without posting a reply first. The reply is the audit trail.
- Don't `--force` push.
- Don't bypass the build/lint/test gate to land "review fixes" — broken main is worse than slow review cycles.
- If a reviewer's concern is wrong, explain why in the reply and resolve. Don't leave open threads festering.
- If you genuinely can't tell what a thread is asking for, ask the user — don't guess and resolve.

```bash
go build -o /tmp/entire-test ./cmd/entire

# Non-interactive path (piped stdin → prints update + rerun commands):
ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR=$(mktemp -d) /tmp/entire-test login --device \
  --insecure-http-auth --server http://127.0.0.1:18571 </dev/null

  --insecure-http-auth --server http://127.0.0.1:18571
```

**Careful with Yes on the interactive prompt** — it really runs the installer (`curl … | bash` for a non-brew binary), which would install/overwrite entire on your machine. Press **No** to see the fallback block, or test the print-only behavior in a TTY with `ENTIRE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1`.

`--device` matters: the browser flow binds a local listener first, so the device flow hits the fake server directly. `--insecure-http-auth` needed for `http://`. Kill server after: `pkill -f fakeas.py`.

To test the refresh-grant path (any command, not just login) you'd need a real logged-in context whose server gates the token endpoint — the fake-AS login test is the practical option.
